span.label: whether the gradually drifting neural state present while a word is studied returns when that word is recalled, and returns with it the states of its list neighbours
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: is there direct neurophysiological evidence for contextual reinstatement, which behavioural work has only supported indirectly
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: finds a neural signature of temporal context reinstatement — recall-time activity resembles study-time activity for the recalled item and, in graded fashion, for its neighbours — and shows its strength predicts each patient's behavioural contiguity effect
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: existence
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: temporal context reinstatement during memory search
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: Recalling an item revives the contextual state bound to it at study, and that retrieved context then cues other items encoded in similar contexts, which is what produces the contiguity effect.
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: A slowly drifting contextual state becomes associated with each event as it is experienced, so that later recall of the event reinstates that state.
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: context is operationalised by a property the theory predicts — slow drift — so the features analysed are exactly those that could carry a context signal
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: the circularity that would create is blocked by splitting selection from test: the filter is fitted on study events only, and the hypothesis is tested on recall events
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: the filter's cost is stated rather than hidden — removing content information also removes the forward asymmetry the behavioural effect shows, so a known feature of the phenomenon is invisible by construction
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: the discriminating prediction is bidirectional decay: content reinstatement alone predicts a forward boost, autocorrelated noise predicts no lag structure, and only context predicts symmetric decay
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: rival accounts are built and run rather than argued against — three neural network simulations using the same presented and recalled items as the real analysis
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: the rehearsal alternative is tested through a consequence it would have elsewhere: if rehearsal drove the effect, neural contiguity should track the primacy effect, and it does not
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: individual differences carry the inference: the same patients supply both the neural measure and the behavioural one, so the two can be correlated across people rather than compared as group means
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: a gradual-drift result is treated as insufficient on its own, because ordinary autocorrelated processes would produce it too
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: only negative lags are used for the reinstatement measure, because forward lags cannot separate content from context
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: the inclusion threshold is justified as an explicit trade-off between dimensionality and sample size rather than presented as a natural cutoff
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: Parietal and occipital results were inconclusive because of insufficient data.
span.note: what this limits: the parietal and occipital results: OUR FINDINGS IN THE PARIETAL AND OCCIPITAL LOBES WERE INCONCLUSIVE DUE TO INSUFFICIENT DATA
Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: Null results outside temporal lobe do not establish that other regions are uninvolved.
span.note: what this limits: the extratemporal null: OUR INABILITY TO FIND NEURAL SIGNATURES OF CONTEXT REINSTATEMENT IN EXTRATEMPORAL BRAIN REGIONS DOES NOT NECESSARILY MEAN THAT THOSE REGIONS ARE NOT INVOLVED IN CONTEXT REINSTATEMENT
Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: The analysis cannot resolve structures within the coarse regions of interest.
span.note: what this limits: any structure-level claim: OUR ANALYSIS DOES NOT DISTINGUISH BETWEEN STRUCTURES CONTAINED WITHIN THE REGIONS OF INTEREST WE EXAMINED
Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: A large share of recording sessions was discarded for having too few candidate context features.
span.note: what this limits: the analysed sample: WE FURTHER EXCLUDED AN ADDITIONAL 68 SESSIONS IN WHICH FEWER THAN FIVE CANDIDATE CONTEXT FEATURES WERE IDENTIFIED
Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: a null in other regions is not read as evidence of absence
span.note: duplicate of: limitations[1] · what this limits: the same scope as item 1 - absence of evidence is not read as evidence of absence
Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: the regions of interest are too coarse to identify a structure

span.label: rehearsal-based and context-based accounts are conceded to be hard to tell apart in principle
span.note: what this limits: any claim that separates the two accounts: REHEARSAL-BASED MODELS HAVE BEEN SHOWN TO BE DIFFICULT TO DISTINGUISH FROM CONTEXT-BASED MODELS
Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: the primacy control rests on rehearsal being the mechanism of primacy, which the paper acknowledges is not settled
span.note: what this limits: the primacy-based control: ALTHOUGH REHEARSAL IS ONE OF THE HYPOTHESIZED MECHANISMS UNDERLYING PRIMACY, WE RECOGNIZE THAT OTHER FACTORS, SUCH AS ENHANCED ATTENTION TO EARLY LIST ITEMS, MAY ALSO CONTRIBUTE TO PRIMACY
Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: Rehearsal-based models → context-based models
span.note: THE TWO CANNOT BE SEPARATED IN THIS STUDY - the DESIGN form (Q-286/Q-287). It bounds what the paper's own results can mean, and it lives in a methods paragraph where nothing downstream will find it. TWO MODEL CLASSES THAT CANNOT BE TOLD APART BY THE DATA, with the reason given: a context-based mechanism is needed to explain the rehearsal pattern, so the two are entangled by construction.

span.label: context — as external environmental conditions versus as an internal, ever-changing mental state; the paper's theory requires both
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: context — operationalised: the principal components whose activity is positively autocorrelated during study, and nothing else
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: reinstatement — of content (the item's own representation) versus of context (the states of its neighbours); the whole design exists to separate these
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: contiguity effect — behavioural (transitions between neighbouring items at recall) versus neural (similarity declining with absolute lag); the paper coins the second and correlates the two
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: contextual features — as environmental cues, as recently studied items, as internal mental states, or as a process evolving randomly; four readings the founding theories left open
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: gradual change — as evidence for context versus as the signature of any autocorrelated process; the paper insists the first requires more than the second
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: method: electrocorticography in epilepsy patients during delayed free recall; oscillatory power in five bands per electrode, reduced by PCA, with components selected for slow autocorrelation during study and tested for similarity to recall-time activity as a function of lag

span.label: Neural similarity between pairs of studied words fell off as the distance between their serial positions grew, showing that the ECoG signal drifts gradually across a list.

span.label: Brain activity recorded just before a word was recalled was more similar to activity during study of that same word than to activity during study of any other list word.
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: Similarity between recall activity and study activity declined with absolute lag in both the forward and backward directions, the pattern predicted by context reinstatement rather than item-content reinstatement.
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: Participants whose neural reinstatement effect was stronger also recalled neighbouring list items successively more often, linking the neural signature to the behavioural contiguity effect.
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: Restricting the analysis to temporal lobe electrodes still produced the graded decrease of similarity with lag in both directions.

span.label: The frontal-lobe reinstatement signature showed no relationship to how strongly participants clustered their recalls in time, unlike the temporal-lobe signature.

span.label: Primacy strength was unrelated to neural contiguity, arguing against rehearsal during study as the source of the reinstatement effect.
